facts.detail: The technical annex was published on 26 June 2026.
The annex provides technical detail supporting the main GigaHub Evaluation Process Review.
It records modelling assumptions, scoping patterns and qualitative evidence-gathering methods.
The model links English primary schools, GP surgeries and libraries to broadband-performance data.
BDUK administrative data covered 2,553 Hubs supported by the programme.
The administrative data included site identity, address, type, connection timing, project and funding body.
Seven snapshots were collected between July 2023 and July 2024.
The snapshots were linked to create a Hub-level panel tracking development over time.
The England modelling combined lists into 28,998 public buildings.
Within the modelled public-building list, 193 were connected through GigaHubs and 570 through RGC.

guard_streams.source: Your right to request a decent broadband service: What you need to know
guard_streams.write_limit: Universal-service eligibility and build-cost rules are consumer rights and cannot be used as evidence that a parcel currently has broadband coverage or a measured speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom lists the broadband universal-service guide as last updated on 19 June 2026.
Every UK home and business has a legal right to request a decent, affordable broadband connection.
A decent connection is defined as at least 10 Mbit/s download and 1 Mbit/s upload.
Eligible requests go to BT, or KCOM in the Hull area, without requiring an existing customer relationship.
Existing fixed-wireless or satellite services may provide an alternative upgrade route.
BT or KCOM has 30 days to confirm eligibility and estimated build cost.
Eligibility requires no access to an existing decent broadband service.
Eligibility also requires that no public broadband scheme will cover the premises within the next 12 months.
A premises with only a decent service priced above £59.60 per month may also request a universal-service connection.
Build costs up to £3,400 are covered; above that threshold the customer pays the excess and receives a survey quote within 60 days.
